title: AID Generation Transaction Manifest
description: The durable manifest that makes one plan's generation ONE transaction. Written as an identity-only skeleton under the transaction lock before the CP1 gate runs, then extended phase by phase. STATUS IS NEVER STORED: a rerun derives each phase's status by re-hashing the recorded outputs and reading queue membership, so the files and the queue are the truth and this manifest is only the binding that lets a rerun verify rather than blindly redo.

plan_path.description: The plan this generation ran from. Used by the queue-add ownership check to prove a transaction-owned duplicate belongs to the same plan the queued entry was added for.

authority_sha256.description: The self_sha256 of the generation authority this transaction was decided under. Null only in the skeleton written before the authority is sealed; every phase verifier requires the match, which is what makes a leaked authority useless outside its own transaction.

phases.description: Map of phase number (as a string key) to that phase's record. Every phase's ids are pre-derived in the skeleton, so the verifier compares a RE-DERIVED id against a RECORDED one; the two hashes stay absent until that phase's outputs exist.

epic_path.description: Where the generated EPIC landed. Recorded so resume can re-hash the exact file rather than guess it back from a slugified title.

plan_json.description: Where the generated plan.json landed (same reason as epic_path).

contract_validate.description: This phase's contract-validation evidence. Resume requires it to still be a pass; a phase whose evidence is gone is regenerated.

queued.description: Set when stage 2 has put this phase's EPIC in the queue — including by the adopt-from-queue path, where a crash between queue-add and the manifest update left the queue ahead of the manifest.
